  "narrative_text": "The metabolomics differential abundance dataset reveals a pronounced perturbation of arachidonic acid metabolism as the dominant biological signal, with cross-paradigm agreement across m/z network (Mummichog) and KEGG-specific ORA (MetaboAnalystR). Mummichog returned Arachidonic acid metabolism as the top-ranked pathway (MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism, p=0.00227, 13/13 metabolites matched), and MetaboAnalystR confirmed arachidonic acid metabolism (KEGG:hsa00590, p=0.106) within its top five. The input lipid mediators—8(S)-HPETE (C14823), 16(R)-HETE (C14778), 19(S)-HETE (C14749), thromboxane A2 (C02198), and 11,12,15-THETA (C14782)—are all structurally consistent with canonical CYP450 and LOX branch metabolism of arachidonic acid. A secondary axis of perturbation involves retinoic acid signaling and one-carbon metabolism. RaMP ORA returned Signaling by Nuclear Receptors (REACT:R-HSA-9006931, FDR=0.00145) as its top hit, driven by 4-hydroxyretinoic acid and S-adenosylmethionine (SAM), the latter also appearing across multiple methylation-related Reactome pathways (PKMTs methylate histone lysines, PRC2 methylates histones and DNA) at the same FDR threshold. Theophylline (C07130), a adenosine receptor antagonist and CYP1A2 substrate, likely contributes to cross-talk between xanthine metabolism and the nuclear receptor axis. Uridine 5'-diphosphate (UDP, C00015) appeared in Mummichog's glycerophospholipid and N-glycan biosynthesis hits, suggesting nucleotide-sugar donor availability may be altered. Sodium chloride (C13563) was retained as a structurally resolved input but carries no informative pathway load. react_result.final_narrative_text: The metabolomics differential abundance dataset reveals a pronounced perturbation of arachidonic acid metabolism as the dominant biological signal, with cross-paradigm agreement across m/z network (Mummichog) and KEGG-specific ORA (MetaboAnalystR). Mummichog returned Arachidonic acid metabolism as the top-ranked pathway (MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism, p=0.00227, 13/13 metabolites matched), and MetaboAnalystR confirmed arachidonic acid metabolism (KEGG:hsa00590, p=0.106) within its top five. The input lipid mediators—8(S)-HPETE (C14823), 16(R)-HETE (C14778), 19(S)-HETE (C14749), thromboxane A2 (C02198), and 11,12,15-THETA (C14782)—are all structurally consistent with canonical CYP450 and LOX branch metabolism of arachidonic acid. A secondary axis of perturbation involves retinoic acid signaling and one-carbon metabolism. RaMP ORA returned Signaling by Nuclear Receptors (REACT:R-HSA-9006931, FDR=0.00145) as its top hit, driven by 4-hydroxyretinoic acid and S-adenosylmethionine (SAM), the latter also appearing across multiple methylation-related Reactome pathways (PKMTs methylate histone lysines, PRC2 methylates histones and DNA) at the same FDR threshold. Theophylline (C07130), a adenosine receptor antagonist and CYP1A2 substrate, likely contributes to cross-talk between xanthine metabolism and the nuclear receptor axis. Uridine 5'-diphosphate (UDP, C00015) appeared in Mummichog's glycerophospholipid and N-glycan biosynthesis hits, suggesting nucleotide-sugar donor availability may be altered. Sodium chloride (C13563) was retained as a structurally resolved input but carries no informative pathway load. The convergent winner is arachidonic acid metabolism, with five HETE/HPETE/THETA species and thromboxane A2 defining the driver-metabolite cluster.
